extracted.intended_audience: DOE and NRC staff, parties, potential parties, interested governmental participants, counsel, and administrators participating in pre-license/high-level radioactive waste repository adjudications under 10 CFR Part 2, subpart J
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and technical rules governing what documentary material must be produced, how it must be formatted and made available via the Licensing Support Network (LSN), and how claims of privilege or classified/Safeguards Information are handled during the pre-license application phase for a geologic repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclassified statements required (§2.910)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever Restricted Data or other National Security Information is introduced into a proceeding, the party offering it shall submit to the presiding officer and to all parties an unclassified statement setting forth the information in the classified matter as accurately and completely as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer shall determine whether the unclassified statement (with any appropriate modifications) may be substituted for the classified matter without prejudice; if unclassified statement adequately sets forth relevant classified information, the presiding officer shall direct that the classified matter be excluded from the record. If not adequate, the presiding officer must state reasons in the record. The presiding officer may rearrange order of proceedings, suspend proceedings (not more than 100 days without consent or finding), or postpone procedures until reception of other evidence is complete. Service of the unclassified statement shall not be postponed if any party lacks access to classified material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of Restricted Data or other National Security Information (§2.911)
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer shall not receive any Restricted Data or other National Security Information in evidence unless: (a) its relevance and materiality to the issues and its competence are clearly established; and (b) exclusion of the information would prejudice the interests of a party or the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both prongs must be satisfied for admission. This is the standard the presiding officer uses to decide whether classified material may be received into evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight to be attached to classified evidence (§2.912)
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering the weight and effect of any Restricted Data or other National Security Information received in evidence to which an interested party has not had opportunity to receive access, the presiding officer and the Commission shall give to such evidence such weight as is appropriate under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into consideration any lack of opportunity to rebut or impeach the evidence when assigning weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and expungement of classified evidence (§2.913)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the close of the reception of evidence, the presiding officer shall review the record and shall direct that any Restricted Data or other National Security Information be expunged from the record where such expunction would not prejudice the interests of a party or the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such directions will be considered by the Commission on review of the presiding officer's determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and precedence of Subpart J (§2.1000)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart, together with subparts C and G, governs the procedure for applications for authorization to construct a high-level radioactive waste repository and for licenses to receive and possess high-level waste; the procedures in this subpart take precedence over specified provisions of subparts C and G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists numerous sections of subparts C and G for which the usual subpart precedence is preserved; practitioners must consult the enumerated exceptions to know when other subparts' provisions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Documentary material' (scope) (§2.1001)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentary material means: (1) any information a party intends to rely on and/or cite in support of its position in the proceeding; (2) any information known to or in possession of the party that is relevant but does not support that party's position; and (3) all reports and studies prepared by or on behalf of the party, including all related 'circulated drafts', relevant to the license application and the Topical Guidelines in Regulatory Guide 3.69, regardless of whether they will be relied upon or cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope of documentary material shall be guided by the topical guidelines in the applicable NRC Regulatory Guide (Topical Guidelines for the Licensing Support System). This definition determines what must be produced to other participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic header requirement (definition and production)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographic header means the minimum series of descriptive fields that a potential party, interested governmental participant, or party must submit with a document or other material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An electronic file including a bibliographic header must be provided for all documentary material (including circulated drafts but excluding preliminary drafts). An authentication statement for posting on the LSN Web site indicating where an authenticated image copy can be obtained must accompany production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document classifications and size thresholds (simple, large, complex)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple document: electronic files 50 megabytes or less. Large document: electronic files larger than 50 megabytes. Complex document: electronic files with substantial non-text content and graphic or other Binary Large Objects exceeding 50 megabytes that cannot logically be divided (e.g., executables, large datasets, software code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification affects how material must be provided (image vs. searchable text) and handling in the LSN; examples of complex documents are provided to guide implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability deadlines for documentary material (§2.1003)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exclusions, DOE shall make material available no later than six months in advance of submitting its license application; NRC shall make available no later than thirty days after DOE certification of compliance; each other potential party, interested governmental participant or party shall make available no later than ninety days after DOE certification of compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The materials to be made available are specified in §2.1003(a)(1)-(4). Timing varies by participant type; practitioners must meet these deadlines for electronic availability on the LSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of content and file formats to be produced (§2.1003 & §2.1011)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required production includes: (a)(1) an electronic file including a bibliographic header for all documentary material (including circulated drafts but excluding preliminary drafts); (a)(2) in electronic image format, subject to privilege claims, graphic-oriented documentary material (raw data, computer runs, programs and codes, field/lab notes, maps, photographs, etc.); (a)(3) bibliographic header only for items not suitable for image or searchable full text; (a)(4) bibliographic header for privileged, confidential financial/commercial, or Safeguards Information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual material must comply with ISO/IEC 8859-1 and be in acceptable formats (ASCII, native word processing, PDF Normal, or HTML). Image files must be TIFF CCITT G4 (bi-tonal) or PNG or PDF(Image) with specified dpi and color depth; images stored as single image-per-page unless server provides page-level access. Bibliographic headers must be programmatically linkable to the text/image file (preferably via hyperlink). Text embedded within graphic-oriented documents need not be separately entered as searchable text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementation obligation (§2.1003(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each potential party, interested governmental participant or party shall continue to supplement its documentary material made available to other participants via the LSN with any additional material created after the time of initial certification until the discovery period in the proceeding has concluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing duty to update the LSN with newly created material during pre-license discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and additions availability timeline (§2.1004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document that has not been provided to other parties in electronic form must be identified in an electronic notice and made available for inspection and copying by the responsible participant within five days after it has been requested unless some other time is approved by the Pre-License Application Presiding Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time allowed will be stayed pending Presiding Officer action on a motion to extend the time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from electronic access (§2.1005)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following material is excluded from the requirement to provide electronic access: official notice materials; reference books and textbooks; material pertaining exclusively to administration (with certain procurement exceptions); press clippings and press releases; junk mail; readily available references cited in contractor reports; classified material subject to subpart I; readily available references subject to copyright; and correspondence with Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories need not be made available via the LSN; parties should consult the list when asserting exclusions from production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privilege claims and handling (§2.1006)
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional discovery privileges recognized in NRC adjudicatory proceedings and exceptions in §2.390 may be asserted. The deliberative process privilege may be asserted by States, local governmental bodies, and Federally-recognized Indian Tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a privilege claim is denied in whole or part, the document must be provided electronically to the other participants or to the Presiding Officer for entry into a Protective Order file. Circulated drafts not otherwise privileged shall be provided for electronic access pursuant to §2.1003(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access locations and public availability (§2.1007)
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic access to the LSN must be provided at DOE headquarters and all DOE Local Public Document Rooms near candidate sites, and at the NRC Web site and/or NRC Public Document Room beginning in the pre-license application phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public availability of paper and electronic copies, duplication fees, and fee waivers are governed by the respective agency regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural responsibilities and certification (§2.1009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participant must: (1) designate an official responsible for administering its obligation to provide electronic files; (2) establish procedures to implement §2.1003; (3) provide staff training on those procedures; (4) ensure all documents carry the submitter's unique identification number; and (5) cooperate with the NRC advisory review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The designated responsible official must certify to the Pre-License Application Presiding Officer that procedures have been implemented and that documentary material has been identified and made electronically available at the time compliance is required; DOE must update this certification when DOE submits the license application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-License Application Presiding Officer: designation and duties (§2.1010)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may designate one or more persons as Pre-License Application Presiding Officer to rule on disputes over electronic availability of documents during the pre-license application phase; designation must occur no later than 15 days after DOE certification of initial compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Presiding Officer shall rule on claims of withholding to determine whether material is within scope, excluded under §2.1005, privileged or otherwise excepted under §2.1006, whether the privilege is absolute or qualified, and if qualified whether disclosure is necessary for a proper decision. The Presiding Officer may order disclosure under a protective order and possesses the general powers specified in §§2.319 and 2.321(c). The Commission will specify the Officer's jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards Information access conditions and protections (§2.1010(b)(6)(i)-(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presiding Officer may order disclosure of Safeguards Information if the individual seeking access has the requisite 'need to know', has undergone an FBI criminal history records check (unless exempt), and OS administration finds the individual trustworthy and reliable (unless exempt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for background checks include fingerprint submission and protections under 10 CFR 73.57 for adverse determinations; individuals may request review of adverse determinations by a designated officer (filing deadlines: requests within 15 days; responses and decisions have specified 10–15 day windows). The Presiding Officer may include any protective terms (including affidavits of nondisclosure). Violations of protective orders may lead to civil penalties (§2.205) and criminal penalties under the Atomic Energy Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for disclosure after final determination (§2.1010(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a final determination that the material is relevant, and not privileged, exempt, or otherwise exempt from production, the participant who asserted the claim of withholding must make the document available in accordance with the provisions of this subpart within five days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures prompt production after denial of withholding claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic document production technical standards (§2.1011(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must obtain systems necessary for electronic document production and comply with design standards: make textual/image versions available on a web-accessible server indexable by crawlers; bibliographic header data must be available in an HTTP-accessible, ODBC/SQL-compliant DBMS or standard database-readable files (XML, CSV); textual material must comply with ISO/IEC 8859-1 and be in acceptable formats; image files must follow specified formats and resolution; bibliographic header must be programmatically linked to its text/image file; participants must adhere to specified network and protocol standards (HTTP/1.1 over TCP/IP, DNS, HTML, SMTP, RFCs for email and MIME).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics include acceptable text formats (ASCII, Word, WordPerfect, PDF Normal, HTML); image formats (TIFF CCITT G4 for bi-tonal; PNG for greyscale/color; PDF image), dpi and color depth minimums, single image-per-page storage recommended, and linkability (preferably via hyperlink) between header and document to facilitate LSN software indexing and retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSN Administrator responsibilities (§2.1011(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Licensing Support Network shall be coordinated by the LSN Administrator, designated before the pre-license application phase, with responsibility to identify technical and policy issues, address LSN Advisory Review Panel advice, identify availability and integrity problems, provide recommendations to resolve problems, provide periodic reports to the Commission, evaluate participant compliance with design standards, provide variances as needed, and issue guidance to participants on compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LSN Administrator must not be within an NRC organizational unit that represents NRC staff as a party; duties include both technical troubleshooting and policy coordination to maintain LSN functionality and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSN Advisory Review Panel composition (§2.1011(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Commission shall reconstitute the LSS Advisory Review Panel as the LSN Advisory Review Panel, composed of the interests currently represented on the LSS Advisory Review Panel; additional representatives may be appointed consistent with the Federal Advisory Committee Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel advises on LSN implementation and provides consensus advice for the LSN Administrator and Commission to consider.
